Statement I: Calls-in-Advance is shown under Current Liabilities under the head 'Other Current Liabilities' in the company Balance Sheet. [Corporate Ref #7]
Statement II: The company is liable to pay interest on Calls-in-Advance even if there are no profits earned during the financial year.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

detailedSolution:

1. Statement I is correct: Under Schedule III of Companies Act 2013, Calls in Advance is presented under Current Liabilities (Other Current Liabilities).
2. Statement II is correct: Interest on calls in advance is a debt liability payable irrespective of whether profits exist.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

Match List-I with List-II
List-I
List-II
(A) Authorized capital
(I) Mentioned in Prospectus
(B) Issued capital
(II) Mentioned in Memorandum Of Association
(C) Subscribed capital. (III) Called up capital – calls in arrears
(D) Paid up capital
(IV) Capital for which application is received
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:

1. (A) Authorized capital: Mentioned in Memorandum of Association -> (II).
2. (B) Issued capital: Mentioned in Prospectus -> (I).
3. (C) Subscribed capital: Capital for which application is received -> (IV).
4. (D) Paid up capital: Called up capital minus calls in arrears -> (III).
5. Correct matching: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).
Hence, option (D) is the correct match.
